open_points.subject: sandbox scratch-limit detection
open_points.text: Only that error is a scratch hit
open_points.question: What observable event makes an execution a scratch-limit hit, especially when agent code catches the write error: any `EFBIG`, only an `EFBIG` proven to result from this execution's `RLIMIT_FSIZE`, or an explicit runner-recorded failed write to the exchange directory?
options: Any observed `EFBIG` raised during agent execution
Only an `EFBIG` from a write to an exchange-directory file at the configured per-file limit
Only an out-of-band event recorded by runner instrumentation, including when code catches the error
open_points.default_guess: Instrument exchange-directory writes and classify `resource_exhausted` only when the runner records a limit-caused `EFBIG`, even if agent code catches it.

open_points.subject: sandbox host-storage exhaustion classification
open_points.text: a write that fails because host storage is exhausted is an ordinary raised error (`crashed` if it escapes `run`)
open_points.question: Which concrete failures count as host-storage exhaustion rather than a scratch hit or internal infrastructure error, and does this rule cover only writes performed inside `run` or also module loading, runner setup, input/output serialization and cleanup writes?
options: `ENOSPC` and quota exhaustion such as `EDQUOT` from agent-code writes during `run`
Any storage-capacity failure anywhere in sandbox setup or execution
open_points.default_guess: Treat `ENOSPC` and `EDQUOT` raised by agent code during module loading or `run` as ordinary Python errors leading to `crashed` when uncaught; treat failures in parent or runner infrastructure as `internal_error`.

open_points.subject: sandbox short or partial writes
open_points.text: a short or partial write is the code's own concern
open_points.question: If a write returns a short count because the per-file limit was reached but raises no error, does the execution remain eligible to succeed, or must it be classified as the scratch `resource_exhausted` limit hit?
options: A short write alone is never a scratch hit; classify from the later execution result
A short write caused by the per-file limit is a scratch hit even without an error
Treat all short writes as scratch hits because their cause is not reliably distinguishable
open_points.default_guess: A short write without the specified error is not a scratch hit; the execution may succeed if all later checks pass.
